The smaller decay root rho increases with m and g since discriminant exceeds corresponding squared numerator by 4beta1*g and 4beta1*m. Second g-derivative -2beta1*m/discriminant^(3/2)<0, so minimum tumor block uses m*=min(m1,m2); min with scalar bottleneck kappa yields full G. Rationalizing root gives rho~(m/(beta1+m))g as g→0, rho=m−beta1*m/g+O(g^-2) at infinity; solving rho=kappa yields gcap=kappa(beta1+m*−kappa)/(m*−kappa) when kappa<m*. Important: global G becomes flat after cap; strict increase only applies to tumor-mode rho, not full capped G.
